items.title: Section: Three Kinds of Pratyekabuddha, from the Convert to the True Hundred-Eon Seeker

items.zh: 獨覺乘證得者，謂略有三種。一、先已得順決擇分善根證得，二、先已得證得證得，三、先未得證得證得。
items.en: Realisation belonging to the pratyekabuddha vehicle is, briefly, of three kinds: realisation for one who has already attained the wholesome roots of the branches conducive to penetration; realisation for one who has already attained direct realisation itself; and realisation for one who has not yet attained realisation at all.

items.zh: 前二證得名為獨勝，最後證得名麟角喻。

items.title: Section: The Bodhisattva's Own Realisation, and a Treatise Describes Its Own Architecture

items.zh: 大乘證得者，謂發心證得、大悲證得、波羅蜜多證得、攝事證得、地證得、於五無量隨至真如證得、不可思議威德信解證得、不共佛法證得等。如是一切，應知如前菩薩地中已廣分別。云何教導？謂由三處所攝教導。一、由藏所攝，二、由摩呾理迦所攝，三、由二所攝。藏所攝者，謂聲聞藏及大乘藏。摩呾理迦所攝者，謂十七地及四種攝。
items.en: Realisation belonging to the Great Vehicle is realisation through arousing the aspiration for awakening, through great compassion, through the perfections, through the means of gathering, through the grounds, through the five infinite spheres and the suchness reached through them, through inconceivable majestic faith and understanding, and through the dharmas unique to buddhas. All of this should be known as already explained at length in the Bodhisattva Grounds. What is teaching? Teaching contained within three categories: within the canon, within the treatise-compendium, and within both. What is contained within the canon is the śrāvaka canon and the Great Vehicle canon. What is contained within the treatise-compendium is the seventeen grounds and the four further compilations.

items.title: Section: Ten Teachings That Together Cover Everything the Treatise Contains

items.zh: 二所攝者，略有十種。謂諦相教、遍知教、永斷教、證得教、修習教、即彼品類差別教、即彼所攝所依能依相屬教、遍知等障法教、遍知等順法教、不遍知等遍知等過失功德教。如是能攝一切藏攝及本母攝，是名總略摩呾理迦。
items.en: What is contained within both is, briefly, of ten kinds: the teaching of the truths' marks, the teaching of full understanding, the teaching of permanent severing, the teaching of realisation, the teaching of cultivation, the teaching of classification of these same truths, the teaching of the relation between what is depended upon and what depends within these same truths, the teaching of the dharmas that obstruct full understanding and the like, the teaching of the dharmas that accord with them, and the teaching of the fault of not fully knowing against the merit of fully knowing. All of this together comprises everything contained within the canon and the treatise-compendium alike, called, in brief, the comprehensive treatise-compendium.

items.title: Section: Sixteen Aspects of the Four Truths, and Twelve Further Kinds of Teaching

items.zh: 復次，教導略有十二。所謂事教、想差別教、觀自宗教、觀他宗教、不了義教、了義教、世俗諦教、勝義諦教、隱密教、顯了教、可記事教、不可記事教。事教者，謂各別說色等、眼等諸法體教。想差別教者，謂廣宣說諸蘊、界、處、緣起、處非處、根、諦等名想差別。
items.en: Furthermore, teaching is, briefly, of twelve kinds: teaching of the matter, teaching of conceptual distinctions, teaching examining one's own tradition, teaching examining other traditions, teaching of provisional meaning, teaching of definitive meaning, teaching of conventional truth, teaching of ultimate truth, hidden teaching, explicit teaching, teaching of what can be answered, and teaching of what cannot be answered. Teaching of the matter names the individual substance of each phenomenon, form and the rest, eye and the rest. Teaching of conceptual distinctions extensively proclaims the conceptual distinctions of the aggregates, elements, sense bases, dependent origination, the possible and impossible, the faculties, and the truths.

items.zh: 又復廣說諸念住等名想差別。又復廣說有色無色、有見無見、有對無對等名想差別。如是無量諸佛世尊廣說諸法想差別教。

items.title: Section: Ten Perfections of a Dharma Teacher, and Speech Sweet Enough to Persuade

items.zh: 觀自宗教者，謂契經、應誦、記別等，依止攝釋宣說開示。
items.en: Teaching examining one's own tradition concerns how the sūtras and other genres are expounded, following the Compendium of Explanations' own guidance. A teacher expounding the Dharma should, through five aspects, explain every Buddhist sūtra in accordance with its own meaning: first briefly stating its essential point, then explaining the circumstances of its arising, then explaining its meaning, then resolving difficulty, and finally clarifying its proper sequence.

items.title: Section: Seven Aspects of Logic for Defeating a Rival's Argument

items.zh: 觀他宗教者，謂七種相。依止因明，摧伏他論，建立己論。七種相者，謂因明中論體、論處所、論據、論莊嚴等，如前廣說。
items.en: Teaching examining other traditions concerns seven aspects, relying on the science of logic to overturn rival doctrines and establish one's own teaching. The seven aspects are, within the science of logic, the nature of debate, the venue of debate, the basis of debate, the ornaments of debate, and so on, as already extensively explained.

items.zh: 不了義教者，謂契經、應誦、記別等，世尊略說其義未了，應當更釋。了義教者，與此相違，應知其相。世俗諦教者，謂諸所有言道可宣，一切皆是世俗諦攝。

items.title: Section: Five Basic Realities, and Teaching That Hides Versus Teaching That Reveals

items.zh: 又諸所有名想言說增上所現謂相、名、分別，如是皆名世俗諦攝。勝義諦教者，謂四聖諦教，及真如、實際、法界等教。隱密教者，謂從多分聲聞藏教。顯了教者，謂從多分大乘藏教。
items.en: Whatever characteristic, name, and discrimination arises through the power of name, concept, and language is entirely included within conventional truth. Teaching of ultimate truth names the four noble truths, together with suchness, reality's limit, and the dharma realm. Hidden teaching refers chiefly to the śrāvaka canon. Explicit teaching refers chiefly to the Great Vehicle canon.

items.title: Section: Fourteen Questions the Buddha Refused to Answer

items.zh: 可記事教者，謂四種法嗢拕南教。即一切行無常，乃至涅槃寂靜，如是等類所有言教。不可記事教者，謂有問言：世間常耶？此不應記，但言我說此不可記。乃至問言：如來死後有耶無耶？此不應記，但言我說此不可記。此中應知四因緣故，宣說如是不可記事。或有無故，不可記別。謂有問言：我於諸蘊為異不異、常無常等。或有能引無義利故，不可記別。如升攝波葉喻經中，如來自言：我所證法乃有爾所，而不宣說。何以故？彼法不能引義利故。或有甚深故，不可記別。謂有問言：我是有耶？此不應記，勿彼即於諸蘊執我，或離諸蘊而執有我。又有問言：我是無耶？此不應記，勿於世俗言說士夫起損減執。如是如來死後有無，乃至非有非無等，皆甚深故，不可記別。或有其相法爾建立，故不可記。謂有問言：諸法真如於彼諸法異不異耶？此不可記。何以故？彼相法爾不可建立異不異故。
items.en: Teaching of what can be answered names the four seals of the Dharma: all formations are impermanent, and so on through nirvana is peace. Teaching of what cannot be answered concerns questions such as whether the world is eternal, which should not be answered, only that this cannot be answered, and so on through whether the Tathāgata exists or does not exist after death, which likewise cannot be answered. As in the Siṃśapā Leaves Sūtra, where the Tathāgata himself declared: what I have realised is as vast as this, yet I do not teach it all, because it brings no genuine benefit.

blocks.text: The treatise describes its own structure, the ways teaching is given, and the fourteen questions the Buddha would not answer.
Master Cháng Bǎi: one who has already seen the path must keep practising; the standard pratyekabuddha gathers merit through a hundred eons.
The canon, the compendium of treatises, and both. Master Cháng Bǎi: the seventeen stages run from the five consciousnesses to the stage without remainder.
Master Cháng Bǎi: a practitioner cultivating the four truths is what relies; the truths are what is relied on.
(Untranslated, 0654b18: the foundations of mindfulness and form, visible and invisible, are explained in endless detail by the Buddhas.)
Seven aspects of logic, overturning others' doctrines and establishing one's own.

Hidden teaching refers chiefly to the śrāvaka canon, explicit to the Great Vehicle canon. Master Cháng Bǎi: because the Buddha did not reveal the store-consciousness to śrāvakas, it is "hidden". (Untranslated, 0654b27: provisional teaching needs further explanation; definitive teaching does not; whatever words can express is conventional truth.)

The treatise defines what must be taught as the four seals; whether the world is eternal is an example of what is set aside. Master Cháng Bǎi: "What I have taught is like this leaf; what I have known is as many as all the leaves on this tree."
The Buddha's silence on the fourteen questions is not ignorance. Some questions do not lead to freedom, and the treatise counts declining them as part of skilful teaching.

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of realisation of the pratyekabuddha vehicle?
options: the grounds of seeing, cultivation, and the ultimate, the same three as the śrāvaka's
solitary, group-dwelling, and rhinoceros-like
already having the wholesome roots of penetration, already having realisation, and not yet having it
lower, middling, and higher wholesome roots
quiz.why: The treatise lists realisation for one who already has the wholesome roots of penetration, one who already has realisation, and one who has not yet attained it. The images of the solitary one are absent from the English and not tested.

quiz.q: Within which three categories is teaching contained?
options: within sūtra, within discipline, and within treatise, the familiar three baskets
within the śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, and Great Vehicle canons
within the canon, within the treatise-compendium, and within both
within the seventeen grounds, four compilations, and matrix
quiz.why: The treatise lists the canon, the treatise-compendium, and both. It then says the canon means the śrāvaka and Great Vehicle canons, while the compendium means the seventeen grounds and the four further compilations.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi say about the pratyekabuddha who already has realisation?
options: already a Buddha appearing as a pratyekabuddha to help worlds without the Dharma
having heat and summit, but no direct realisation in this life
abiding in the lineage, gathering requisites at the stage of liberation
already past seeing, at least a stream-enterer, who then practises the truths to become an arhat
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: having realised means one has already seen the path, attaining at least the first fruit, yet must continue practising the truths and six skills to become an arhat. The other two descriptions match the first and third kinds.

quiz.q: Which type is the standard pratyekabuddha, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: one already holding the roots of penetration, so deep that this life must bring success
one not yet realised, abiding in the lineage and always gathering requisites at the stage of liberation
one who already has at least the first fruit
one born in a Buddha's age who hears the teaching
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this practitioner is the standard pratyekabuddha, abiding in that lineage and always at the stage of liberation, continually gathering requisites and drawing near the Dharma.

quiz.q: Which four divisions does Master Cháng Bǎi name as the four compilations?
options: the Grounds of Hearing, Reflection, Cultivation, and Bodhisattvas
the sūtra, discipline, treatise, and miscellaneous baskets
the aggregates, elements, sense bases, and dependent origination
Decisive Discernment, Explanation, Synonyms, and Topics
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the seventeen grounds run from the Ground of the Five Consciousnesses to the Ground without Remainder, and the four compilations are Decisive Discernment, Explanation, Synonyms, and Topics, together forming the Yogācārabhūmi.

quiz.q: Which group belongs among the ten kinds contained within both?
options: teaching of the matter, of distinctions, of both traditions, and of provisional meaning
teaching of the truths' marks, full understanding, severing, realisation, and cultivation
true meaning, realisation, teaching, the extremes, the inconceivable
the two canons, the grounds, the compilations, and the matrix
quiz.why: The treatise's ten begin with the truths' marks, full understanding, severing, realisation, and cultivation. The teaching of the matter and the rest belong to the next list of twelve, and true meaning and the rest are the six gateways.

quiz.q: How does the teaching of the matter differ from that of conceptual distinctions?
options: the first teaches daily affairs and community rules, the second the various delusions of ordinary people
the first is for śrāvakas; the second for the Great Vehicle
the first can be answered; the second cannot
the first names each phenomenon's substance; the second proclaims the distinctions of aggregates and so on
quiz.why: The treatise says the teaching of the matter speaks individually of the substance of form, eye, and other phenomena, while the teaching of conceptual distinctions extensively proclaims the aggregates, elements, bases, and so on.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi map support and dependent in this teaching?
options: the support is the storehouse consciousness and the dependent the seven forms of consciousness
the support is the person, and the dependent is the Dharma of the four truths
the support is sūtra, and the dependent treatise
the support is the Buddha, and the dependent the disciple
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: what is relied upon is the person, and what relies is the Dharma of the four truths. A practitioner cultivating the four truths is called the teaching of the relation between support and dependent.

quiz.q: What does teaching examining other traditions rely on, and for what purpose?
options: relying on the science of logic to overturn rival doctrines and establish one's own teaching
relying on the Compendium of Explanations to expound the sūtras and genres
relying on the four truths to cut affliction
relying on absorption to draw forth powers
quiz.why: The treatise says this teaching has seven aspects, relying on logic to overturn others' doctrines and establish one's own. Relying on the Compendium of Explanations is the teaching about one's own tradition.

quiz.q: What does the treatise say of hidden and explicit teaching?
options: hidden teaching is chiefly the Great Vehicle canon and explicit teaching chiefly the śrāvaka canon
hidden teaching is mantra; explicit teaching is sūtra
hidden teaching is chiefly the śrāvaka canon; explicit teaching chiefly the Great Vehicle canon
the first is wholly śrāvaka; the second wholly Great Vehicle, without exception
quiz.why: The treatise says hidden teaching refers chiefly to the śrāvaka canon and explicit teaching chiefly to the Great Vehicle canon. The word chiefly rules out any claim that the division is absolute.

quiz.q: Why does Master Cháng Bǎi say the śrāvaka canon counts as hidden?
options: śrāvaka sūtras were passed secretly among monks and kept from householders, a rule of the early schools which the lecturer explains is the reason the canon is called hidden
its language is Pāli, which ordinary people cannot read
it speaks of powers and not of principles
the Buddha did not reveal the storehouse consciousness to śrāvakas, so from the Great Vehicle view it is hidden
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: because the World-Honoured One did not reveal the principle of the storehouse consciousness to śrāvaka practitioners, it is called hidden teaching from the standpoint of the Great Vehicle.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain what appears through name, concept, and language?
options: words the Buddha displays in the air by power to guide beings, so that whatever the Buddha displays is conventional
marks, names, and discriminations appearing on the basis of name and concept are all conventional truth
what the five senses directly perceive
the light seen in concentration
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: all the marks, names, and discriminations appearing on the basis of name, concept, and speech are included in conventional truth. The first sentence of this teaching is missing from the English, so the opening has nothing to attach to.

quiz.q: What does the treatise mean by teaching of what can be answered?
options: the four seals: all formations are impermanent, and so on through nirvana is peace
whether the world is eternal or the Tathāgata exists after death
cause and effect across the three times
the seventeen grounds and four compilations
quiz.why: The treatise defines it as the four seals, from all formations being impermanent through nirvana being peace. Whether the world is eternal is its example of what cannot be answered.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi present the leaf simile?
options: what is taught is like the whole tree and what is known like one leaf
falling leaves are impermanence; new leaves are nirvana
roots are precepts; leaves are wisdom
what is taught is like these few leaves; what is known is like all the leaves of the tree
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: what I have taught is like this leaf; what I have known is as many as all the leaves on this tree, yet I teach only this little. The treatise gives the reason: it brings no benefit.
